data.name: UnitCallReleaseStatusHelp
data.value: Set, by meaning in the same way, on the units still working a call when it is closed or they are taken off it. A unit already back in service, out of service (unavailable, maintenance or on a break) or working another call keeps its status; custom statuses are read by their base type. Default sets the unit's back-in-service status (Cleared, Available or In Quarters) on custom statuses and Released on the built-in statuses.

data.name: UnitDefaultStatusesHelp
data.value: Set on the units dispatched to a call. Pick what the status means: each unit gets the status of its own status set with that meaning (the first by order), so one setting works for unit types with different custom statuses. Default sets Dispatched (or Responding, or En Route) on units with custom statuses and Responding on units with the built-in statuses.

data.name: UnitTypeStatusOverridesHelp
data.value: Only unit types with custom unit statuses appear here. Pick one of a unit type's own statuses when it needs a specific one; Default uses the department-wide setting above, matched against the unit type's statuses.

data.name: TtsLanguageHelp
data.value: Select the eSpeak-NG language or dialect to use for this department's voice prompts.

data.name: EnableModernNotificationsHelp
data.value: When enabled, push notifications will use the modern notification sounds instead of the legacy sounds for all users in this department.

data.name: ForceChatbotSecurityPinHelp
data.value: Require every member to confirm dangerous or department-wide assistant/text actions with their personal 4-digit security PIN. Members without a PIN get a randomly generated one (viewable on their profile page).

data.name: RunCardDetachedReferencesRemoved
data.value: {0} item(s) on this run card pointed at unit types, roles, call types, stations or statuses that have since been deleted, and were removed. Review the card and save it to keep the change.

data.name: DefaultMapCenterHelp
data.value: Every map in Resgrid and the mobile apps opens here. Leave both blank and we will work it out from the department address above the next time you save; fill them in to pin an exact spot, which is never overwritten.

data.name: NewCallFieldsHelp
data.value: Choose which built-in fields appear on the new call form and which must be completed before a call can be created and sent to the field. Name, nature, priority and type are always shown and always required. The same rules apply when a call is edited or an archived call is added.

data.name: UnitStatusThresholdsHelp
data.value: Highlight a unit on the Big Board when it has been sitting in a status too long — for example, dispatched for more than four minutes without reporting that it has departed. Leave both columns at 0 to time nothing.

data.name: RequirePasswordResetViaEmailHelp
data.value: Prevents department and group administrators from choosing or seeing a member's new password. Reset actions send the member a short-lived, single-use email link instead. Existing sessions are revoked after the member successfully changes the password.

data.name: ProfileIntro
data.value: This is the identity Resgrid prints on records, shows on branded emails and uses wherever the department presents itself. Leave a field empty to fall back to the department settings.

data.name: ProfileAddressNote
data.value: The address printed on records and emails is the department address:

data.name: ProfileLogoHelp
data.value: PNG or JPEG, up to 2 MB, at least 200 px on the long edge (512 px or larger recommended). The upload is re-encoded with its metadata removed, and the print header, email masthead and thumbnail renditions are generated from it.

data.name: ProfileNoLogo
data.value: No logo has been uploaded. Prints and emails use the department name alone.

data.name: ProfileUseBrandingInEmails
data.value: Use the department masthead on operational emails

data.name: ProfileUseBrandingInEmailsHelp
data.value: Call, message, report delivery and workflow emails show your logo and name instead of the Resgrid masthead; records notifications are sent as "department name via Resgrid". Account and billing emails always stay Resgrid-branded.

data.name: ProfileMediaKeyHelp
data.value: Email clients cannot sign in, so the masthead is served from this unguessable link. Regenerating it invalidates the image in every email already sent.

data.name: ProfileLogoRequired
data.value: Choose a PNG or JPEG file to upload.

data.name: ProfileKeyRegenerated
data.value: A new masthead link has been issued; previously sent emails will no longer show the logo.

data.name: ProfileSaveFailed
data.value: The profile could not be saved; check the highlighted fields.

data.name: GroupDispatchScopeEnabledHelp
data.value: When on, each member's active call lists, maps and nearest unit board show only their own group and the groups beneath it: calls inside those groups' boundaries or dispatched to them, plus any call the member reported or was dispatched to. Department admins and the roles below keep a department-wide view. Nothing is copied or moved, so handing dispatch to another desk at shift change is only a change of role.

data.name: GroupDispatchScopeRolesHelp
data.value: Members holding any of these roles (for example a central dispatch center) see every area while scoping is on. Assign or remove the role to hand dispatch over; it takes effect on their next page load.

data.name: GroupDispatchScopeNoRoles
data.value: No personnel roles are defined yet.

data.name: MapStyleHelp
data.value: The base map your department sees on every map in Resgrid: the website, Dispatch, Responder, Unit, IC and BigBoard.

data.name: MapStyleWebsiteUnavailable
data.value: This Resgrid server has no Mapbox token for the website, so website maps keep the standard map. The style you choose still applies in the apps.

data.name: MapStyleOverrideActive
data.value: The Department Mapbox Override below is on, so the website and the apps use that custom style instead of the styles chosen here.

data.name: MapStyleDayHelp
data.value: Used on the website, and in the apps when the device is in light mode.

data.name: MapStyleNightHelp
data.value: Used in the apps when the device is in dark mode. Automatic picks the night version of the day style.

data.name: MapStyleCommunityHelp
data.value: Community styles are designer maps from the Mapbox gallery; several show little street detail, so check the preview before using one for dispatch.

data.name: RunCardTriggerRequired
data.value: Add at least one trigger before saving this run card.

data.name: InQuartersTurnoutHelp
data.value: Time a unit at its station needs before it is moving. Applies to units in an In Quarters status and to units with no GPS position (taken to be at their station). Added to the travel time when ranking closest units. 0 = none.

data.name: MobileTurnoutHelp
data.value: Time a unit that is already out and available needs before it is moving to a new call. Applies to units ranked from their GPS position. Added to the travel time when ranking closest units. 0 = none.

data.name: StatusHoldToConfirmHelp
data.value: In the Unit and Responder apps, crews press and hold a status button for two seconds to set it, instead of tapping it and then pressing Next or Submit. Prevents accidental taps and forgotten confirmations. A status that needs a note or a destination choice still opens its next step.

data.name: CloseCallWhenUnitsClearLabel
data.value: Close call when last unit clears

data.name: CloseCallWhenUnitsClearHelp
data.value: An active call closes on its own when the last unit dispatched to it reports back in service or out of service (a status whose base type is Available, In Quarters, Cleared, Unavailable or Maintenance). Every other dispatched unit must also have reported finished since its dispatch. Only units count: a call with no unit dispatched, a call under an active incident command, or a unit still returning or transporting keeps the call open for the dispatcher.

data.name: CallNumberingIntro
data.value: How new calls are numbered. Changing the pattern never renumbers calls that already have a number.

data.name: CallNumberPatternHelp
data.value: Fixed text (letters, digits, - _ . /) around tokens: {YYYY} or {YY} the year, {MM} the month, {DD} the day and {SEQ} the sequence, which must appear once. The sequence starts again at 1 whenever the date in the number changes: each year with a year, each month with {MM}, each day with {DD}, and never without a date. {MM} needs a year and {DD} needs {MM}. Dates use the department's time zone.

data.name: CallNumberSequenceWidthHelp
data.value: Pads the sequence with leading zeros, so 4 writes 0153. 1 writes it without padding, as Resgrid always has.

data.name: CallNumberRaiseToHelp
data.value: For departments continuing numbers issued before Resgrid: the next call receives this sequence. It can only be raised, never lowered, so a number is never issued twice. Leave it blank to keep the current sequence.

data.name: CallNumberRaiseConfirm
data.value: Raise the next call number? It can only be raised, never lowered.

data.name: CallNumberPatternInvalid
data.value: The call numbering was not saved. The pattern needs {SEQ} exactly once, can only contain letters, digits, - _ . / and the {YYYY}, {YY}, {MM} and {DD} tokens, needs a year for {MM} and {MM} for {DD}, and can be at most 40 characters.

data.name: CallNumberNextBelowCurrent
data.value: The next call number was not raised: it can only be raised above the number the next call already receives ({0}).

data.name: CallNumberNextPatternChanged
data.value: The next call number was not raised because the pattern or the numbering year start changed in the same save. Raise it again for the new sequence.

data.name: CallNumberYearLabelEndYear
data.value: Named by the year it ends in

data.name: CallNumberYearLabelStartYear
data.value: Named by the year it starts in

data.name: CallNumberYearStartHelp
data.value: For calls numbered by a fiscal year, pick the day it starts. A yearly pattern starts again at 1 that day, and {YYYY} and {YY} write the fiscal year's name. Most fiscal years are named by the year they end in, so one starting November 1, 2026 is 2027. January 1 is the calendar year. Patterns with {MM} or {DD} always follow the calendar.

data.name: CallNumberResetsYearlyOn
data.value: Starts again at 1 each year on {0}.

data.name: CallNumberYearStartInvalid
data.value: The call numbering was not saved. The numbering year has to start on a day every year has, so February 29 cannot be used.

data.name: DocumentNumberingIntro
data.value: How Resgrid numbers work orders, invoices, bids and daily time reports. Leave a pattern blank to keep the built-in numbers. Changing a pattern never renumbers documents that already have a number, and a new pattern carries on after any number it would repeat.

data.name: DocumentNumberingYearStartHelp
data.value: For documents numbered by a fiscal year, pick the day it starts. Work order numbers, and patterns with a year, start again at 1 that day, and {YYYY} and {YY} write the fiscal year's name. Most fiscal years are named by the year they end in, so one starting November 1, 2026 is 2027. January 1 is the calendar year. Call and Records numbers have their own year start.

data.name: DocumentNumberPatternHelp
data.value: Fixed text (letters, digits, - _ . /) around {YYYY} or {YY}, {MM}, {DD} and {SEQ}, which must appear once. A pattern with a year starts again at 1 each numbering year; with {MM} or {DD}, each month or day. A number of digits alone is shown with # in front, as invoice, bid and time report numbers always have been.

data.name: DocumentNumberingPartlySaved
data.value: The rest of the document numbering was saved.

data.name: DocumentNumberingYearStartInvalid
data.value: The document numbering was not saved. The numbering year has to start on a day every year has, so February 29 cannot be used.

data.name: DocumentNumberingPatternsRejected
data.value: These patterns were not saved because they are not valid or could write a number longer than 50 characters; those documents kept the numbering they had:

data.name: DocumentNumberingBelowCurrent
data.value: A next number can only be raised. These were left unchanged because the number entered was below the one they will issue next:

data.name: DocumentNumberingNotApplied
data.value: The pattern or the numbering year start changed in the same save, so the next numbers entered were not applied. Raise them again for the new sequence.

data.name: NewCallFieldCannotBeRequired
data.value: A plus code only finds the location and is not saved on the call, so it cannot be required. Require GPS Coordinates instead.

data.name: DeleteDepartmentRecordsWarning
data.value: This department uses Records. When the deletion runs, every record, incident report and attachment, with its history, is permanently deleted; retention periods do not delay it. Export anything you are required to keep before then, or place a legal hold: an active legal hold stops the deletion until it is released.

data.name: DeleteDepartmentLegalHoldWarning
data.value: {0} active legal hold(s) cover this department's Records. The deletion will not run until every hold is released.

data.name: TerminologyIntro
data.value: Use your department's own words. A name set here replaces Resgrid's name for that module or record type in the navigation, on page titles, wherever record types are listed and in the Responder, Unit, IC and Dispatch apps, for every member and in every language. Only the label changes: permissions, links and integrations are not affected. Leave a box empty to keep Resgrid's name.

data.name: TerminologyModulesHelp
data.value: Shown in the navigation, as the title of the module's main page and in the apps' menus. Sentences elsewhere that mention a module keep Resgrid's wording.

data.name: TerminologyRecordTypesHelp
data.value: The built-in Records and Logs types, wherever a type is chosen, listed, printed or exported. To add a type of your own, such as Public Education, create a record definition.

data.name: TerminologyTooLong
data.value: Names can be at most {0} characters; longer names were not saved and are shown for correcting.

data.name: TerminologyInvalidCharacters
data.value: Names cannot contain < > { or }; those names were not saved and are shown for correcting.

data.name: UnitStatusTargetNoMatch
data.value: {0}: its status set "{1}" has no status meaning {2}, so its units keep their status on {3}. Set a base type on one of its statuses, or pick one in the overrides below.

data.name: UnitStatusTargetSeveral
data.value: {0}: its status set "{1}" has {2} statuses meaning {3} ({4}); {5}, the first by order, is used on {6}.

data.name: UnitStatusTargetNoBuiltIn
data.value: {0}: the built-in unit statuses have none meaning {1}, so its units keep their status on {2}.

data.name: UnitStatusAlertNoteRequirementHelp
data.value: Whether a dispatcher must enter a reason when acknowledging or muting a status timer alert on the Big Board. The reason stays with the alert for follow-up on recurring delays.

data.name: UnitStatusTimerDispatchNoMeaning
data.value: On dispatch, {0} go to "{1}", which has no meaning, so dispatched units are never timed. Give "{1}" a meaning (for example Dispatched) in Custom Statuses.

data.name: UnitStatusTimerDispatchNoTimer
data.value: On dispatch, {0} go to "{1}" ({2}), but no timer is set for {2}.

data.name: UnitStatusTimerSetNoMeaning
data.value: Status set "{0}" (used by {1}) has statuses with no meaning, which no timer can apply to: {2}.

data.name: UnitStatusOverrideNoMeaning
data.value: {0}: the override sets "{1}" on {2}, but that status has no meaning, so status timers, release rules and run cards can't recognise it. Give it a meaning in Custom Statuses.

data.name: OrgTypeHelp
data.value: Describes your organization. Every template, pack and module stays available whichever type you choose.

data.name: OrgTypeProfileHint
data.value: Does your organization do several kinds of work? Select every sector that applies in the operating profile to get setup suggestions for each.

data.name: OrgTypeInvalid
data.value: Choose an organization type from the list.

data.value: Status meaning (your status with this meaning)

data.name: ResetTargetSetsNow
data.value: This choice was saved earlier and is no longer offered. The daily reset currently sets everyone to {0}. Pick a meaning or one of your own options and save to change it.

data.name: ResetTargetSetsNobody

data.name: RunCardRelaxUnfilledRowsLabel
data.value: Relax status filters for unfilled rows

data.name: RunCardRelaxUnfilledRowsHelp
data.value: When a row's status filter finds nothing, propose the fastest available unit of the same kind instead.

data.name: RunCardWaitingAutoDispatchLabel
data.value: Dispatch freed units to calls awaiting them

data.name: RunCardWaitingAutoDispatchHelp
data.value: Overrides the department setting for calls this card leaves awaiting a resource.

data.name: RunCardDecisionGraphHelp
data.value: A level can ask questions (which unit arrives first, is one available in time) and propose the response package of the outcome it reaches. Its rows above are always sent.

data.name: ResponsePackagesHelp
data.value: A response package is a named set of resources (for example "Engine and ambulance") that run card levels and decision outcomes send. Changing a package changes every card that uses it.

data.name: ResponsePackageRowsHelp
data.value: Each row accepts any of its resource types. A substitute package fills what a row could not, and "keep outstanding" makes the call keep awaiting the original resource.

data.name: PersonnelTurnoutHelp
data.value: Added to a person's travel time when run card rows that accept people compare them with units.

data.name: WaitingCallAutoDispatchLabel
data.value: Dispatch freed units to calls awaiting them

data.name: WaitingCallAutoDispatchHelp
data.value: Off: dispatchers are alerted when a matching unit becomes available. On: the unit is sent to the highest-priority waiting call automatically. Run cards can override this.

data.name: WaitingCallMaxResponseHelp
data.value: A freed unit further away than this is alerted, not sent. The alert itself always fires.

data.name: ResponseCodesHelp
data.value: Optional per-unit codes for run card proposals, such as C3 for lights and siren. Leave empty to keep codes out of every screen.

data.name: ResponseCodesShowToCrewsLabel
data.value: Show codes to crews (unit push and field apps)

data.name: AwaitingResourcesHelp
data.value: Active calls still waiting for a resource their run card required but that was not available when they were dispatched. A call leaves this list when a matching resource is sent, a dispatcher dismisses the requirement, or the call is closed.

data.name: AwaitingDismissPrompt
data.value: Why is this resource no longer needed? (optional)

data.name: RunCardTemplatesHelp
data.value: Start from a working card. Templates name resources by meaning, so they map onto your unit types and roles; review the result, test it, then enable it.

data.name: RunCardTemplatesSetClasses
data.value: {0} unit type(s) have no class, so templates can only match them by name.

data.name: RunCardTemplateAppliedMessage

data.name: RunCardSelectionsGuideDefault
data.value: Most run cards can leave this tab empty. With nothing selected the card uses the standard availability rules: units and personnel whose status counts as available or delayed, and staffing levels that count as available, on shift or delayed.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsGuideReplace
data.value: Selecting anything in a section replaces the standard rules for that section: only what you select counts as available, and everything else is skipped.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsGuideStart
data.value: To widen the standard rules, click "Start from the standard rules" and then tick the extra statuses, for example Returning, so units heading back from another call can still be recommended.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsGuideMeanings
data.value: Prefer status meanings to individual statuses. A meaning matches every status with that meaning, built-in or your own, including statuses you add later.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsUnitsHelp
data.value: Set one rule for all unit types, then customize a unit type only when it needs something different. A customized unit type uses only its own selections.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsAllUnitTypesHelp
data.value: Applies to every unit type that is not customized below.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsPersonnelHelp
data.value: Which personnel statuses count as available for this card.

data.name: RunCardSelectionsStaffingHelp
data.value: Which staffing levels count as available. A person must pass both the personnel status rule and the staffing level rule.
